notes.1: This question was well answered by candidates with part (b) producing better results than part (a).
notes.2: Most candidates achieved 2 marks out of the 4 marks that were available.
notes.5: This question was quite well answered, part (a) was not as well answered as part (b).
notes.6: Candidates produced some good answers. Many candidates stated about the forum not being monitored and that it allowed freedom of speech.
notes.8: Many candidates wrote good answers about the questionnaires and interviews but struggled with evaluating these elements. Many candidates managed to achieve two of the marks for the question.
notes.9: This question overall was fairly well answered especially parts (a) and (b).
notes.10: This question related to the use of eSafety strategies and social media. As with previous questions of this type some candidates did not give enough detail in their answers or repeated the same points.
notes.11: Both parts of this question were well answered producing some good answers.
notes.1a: The question was well answered with many candidates able to give answers of devices that were part of a tablet computer rather than devices that could be attached to a tablet computer.
notes.1b: This part of the question was answered better than part (a).
notes.3a: Many candidates who gave answers related to generic software rather than expert systems. There were a large number of brand names given by the candidates that achieve no mark.
notes.3b: Many candidates give answers relating directly to computers rather than expert systems.
notes.4a: Many candidates incorrectly answered with data types rather than validation checks.
notes.4bi: This was well answered by many of the candidates who gave the correct name of the field. As in previous examination series as the name was listed in the question the spelling had to be correct to achieve the mark.
notes.4bii: This was better answered than part (i) but as with the first part it was important that the name of the field was correct in order to achieve the mark.
notes.4c: Many candidates were able to achieve the mark for this part, however some candidates thought that it could not be an integer due to its length. The answers the examiners were looking for was the leading zero or the fact that it was not used in calculations.
notes.4d: Many candidates achieved marks for the checking of the date and the creation and sending of the email rather than the technical side of the database.
notes.5a: This topic had been set in previous examination series where the answers given in those series were good.
notes.5b: This part of the question was very well answered with many candidates able to identify good methods.
notes.7a: This question dealt with the computer processing and contactless cards. Some candidates appear to have misread the question and stated input and outputs relating to the topic as well as the processing.
notes.7b: Some candidates found the question quite challenging achieving only two marks out of a possible six. As with other questions of this type the way to achieve higher marks is to write a detailed answer rather than bullet points.
notes.7c: Some candidates missed out the question, whilst others made an attempt but did not expand on their answer. There was a range of incorrect answers for the abbreviation SSL.
notes.7d: In this question https://was well answered with most candidates either writing that it was a protocol or that it was secure. The second part was well answered by most stating it was the name of the bank or the domain name, although some thought it referred to the web address. The .com part was not well answered.
notes.9a: This question was well answered with general hardware for virtual reality; however few candidates gave specialist equipment like steering wheels. Fewer candidates wrote computer and keyboard which are far too vague.
notes.9b: Most candidates were able to achieve at least one mark on this part of the question. Virtual reality is a harder concept for candidates to write about, but the answers are getting better compared to previous examination series.
notes.9c: Many candidates understood the concept of corporate house styles, but answers lacked detail. The examiners were looking for answers that clearly explained that using corporate house style meant that the documents are from the same company as they have the same format. Some candidates wrote about the house style making the company more professional.
notes.11a: Those candidates that gave the technical answer wrote that the image would become pixelated whereas others wrote that the quality of the image would be reduced, both answers were correct. This question was well answered with most candidates achieving the mark.
notes.11b: This question produced some good answers with many candidates achieving three of the five marks available. Candidates were able to explain how cropping could be carried either removing the unwanted area or selecting the area that was required. Some candidates, however, lacked detail in their answers.
notes.12a: Candidates wrote about conditional formatting, but some answers lacked detail. Again, as with previous questions of this type the way to achieve higher marks is to give clear, detailed answers.
notes.12b: Good answers relating to replication achieved marks as did easy to remember the name rather than the range.
notes.12c: The answers given tended not to use the named range but wrote the range out in full, in some cases this range was incorrect therefore not achieving marks. Some candidates produced a very good answer, but others could not produce enough detail relating to the index number.
notes.12d: This question was well answered. Many candidates explained how the graph was drawn and give a good improvement. As the improvement was part of the question those candidates that did not give an improvement could not achieve full marks.
notes.12e: This question was very well answered by candidates. Many filled the space available with all the elements and produced very good layouts that could be printed out. INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY
